Biotin report

2026-08-05

Samples: biotin was compared across LK1 and LK2, and the high/low split was done on WEI21_26-17_NK from LK3.

Status: the labelling works. The high-versus-low split is exploratory.

Analysis finished: 2026-08-05 - the most recent of the 49 figures shown below.

Report generated: 2026-08-05 by 04.biotin_report.Rmd, from the outputs of steps 01-03 in this folder.

Biotin is carried on the ADT panel as a readout of cell-surface glycosylation - “sugar-seq”. It was added deliberately from the pilot run onward, so every CITE-seq experiment carries it alongside the antibody panel. This report covers how much biotin signal there is, how it is distributed, and what separates biotin-high from biotin-low cells.

For full report, download biotin_report.html in the attachment and open in a browser.

Code used - attached and in the github repository: https://github.com/nbartonicek/surface_proteome_dev/tree/main/lab_archives/6.Biotin_report

Aim

  • does the biotin labelling work at all, and is it consistent between runs
  • how is biotin distributed across cell types
  • what distinguishes biotin-high from biotin-low cells within one population

Conclusions

  • sugar-seq worked - biotin signal is present and structured in every sample, not uniform noise
  • biotin is strongly cell-type dependent. Monocytes carry markedly the most, with pro-monocytes and cDC next; lymphoid populations and erythroid precursors carry the least. The pattern holds in both normal donors and the AML sample
  • the signal is spatially coherent on the projected UMAP rather than scattered, which is what rules out its being a technical artefact of the ADT panel
  • within HSC/MPP, splitting on biotin gives differences in RNA, in surface protein and in cell-cycle phase, but this arm is exploratory - it has been run on one sample only
  • the same split in monocytes runs but on only 160 cells, and does not separate cycling from non-cycling: both groups are ~90% G1
  • glycosylation has to be read against total surface load: step 02 computes CITE residuals adjusted for that, because otherwise a cell with more surface protein of any kind looks more glycosylated

1. Does it work, and is it consistent

Step 01 compares biotin ADT levels between the LK1 and LK2 runs. It was split out of the broader HTO/ADT comparison so it can be run without the demultiplexing steps.

test_biotin_reads_before_after.pdf

Biotin ADT compared across the LK1 and LK2 runs.

test_biotin_reads_per_cell_before_after.pdf

Biotin ADT compared across the LK1 and LK2 runs.

biotin_umap_per_sample.png

Biotin on the projected UMAP for the two normal donors and the AML sample. The signal concentrates in the same region of the map in all three, which is the evidence that the labelling worked - a technical artefact would not localise consistently to one part of the manifold across independent samples.

2. Distribution across cell types

biotin_by_celltype_violin.png

Biotin by broad cell type, split by sample. Monocytes are the clear outlier, with pro-monocytes and cDC behind them; Pro-B, Pre-B and late erythroid sit lowest. The ordering is the same in normal-02, normal-CD34-01 and WEI21_26-17_NK, so it tracks cell identity rather than sample or disease state.

3c_glyco_by_fine_celltype_violin.pdf

The same picture at the fine cell type level, from step 02.

3. Biotin-high versus biotin-low in HSC/MPP

Step 02 takes the HSC/MPP compartment, splits it on CITE_DSB biotin, and asks what else differs. Everything in this section is one sample, WEI21_26-17_NK.

3b. The same split in monocytes

Monocytes carry the most biotin, so they are the obvious population to split. This arm had never been run - the report script existed but nothing wrote the object it needs. Step 02a is step 02 with the population taken as an argument; run as Rscript 02a.biotin_split_analysis_runnable.R "Monocyte" it produced everything below.

The population is small. 160 monocytes pass QC in this sample, splitting 80 high and 80 low at the median. That is a tenth of the HSC/MPP compartment, and it is why the pseudobulk contrast here is thinner - treat the gene-level results as indicative only.

Two differences from the HSC/MPP outputs are worth noting rather than glossing. This run writes its UMAPs into a umaps/ subdirectory while the HSC/MPP figures sit flat, and it produces no edgeR volcano where HSC/MPP has one - both because the HSC/MPP outputs came from an earlier version of the analysis script than the one frozen here as step 02.

4. What was run, in order

Step Script What it does
01 01.biotin_ADT_comparison.R Biotin ADT compared across the LK1 and LK2 runs.
02a 02a.biotin_split_analysis_runnable.R Step 02 with the population as an argument, so any cell type can be split. Used to produce the monocyte arm.
02 02.hsc_mpp_biotin_split_analysis.R HSC/MPP split on biotin, then RNA DE, fgsea, pseudobulk, CITE DE, glycosylation by cell type, surface-load residuals, cell cycle.
03 03.biotin_split_report.Rmd The report over step 02’s outputs.
04 04.biotin_report.Rmd This report.

Three scripts are not kept as separate steps. scripts/27b.hsc_mpp_biotin_split_report.Rmd is the longer first version of step 03 and is superseded by it. scripts/27d.monocyte_biotin_split_report_short.Rmd is step 03 pointed at monocytes, differing by three lines - the title and two paths. It could not run before because nothing wrote the object it reads; step 02a now does, so it is reproducible. scripts/27.removeme_quick_biotin_test.R is scratch, named by its author as disposable.

7. Caveats

  1. The high/low split is one sample. Everything in section 3 comes from WEI21_26-17_NK alone, so the RNA and protein differences are not replicated. Treat them as hypotheses.
  2. The monocyte arm rests on 160 cells, 80 high and 80 low. It has now been run, but that is a tenth of the HSC/MPP compartment, so its gene-level results are weaker still.
  3. Both DESeq2 and edgeR volcanoes are shown rather than one, because with a single sample the pseudobulk dispersion is fixed rather than estimated and the two methods can disagree.
  4. The cross-run comparison is LK1 against LK2 only. LK3, which supplied the split sample, is not in it.
